In a video statement Saturday morning, Michael Kotlikoff also acknowledged that there are troubling questions about the initial investigation.

Americans could see some relief from high fuel prices after the G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel from emergency reserves.
But as NPR's Windsor Johnston reports, that relief might be short-lived.
Americans could see diesel prices start to ease this month as emergency fuel reserves reach the market.
Tom Closa, chief energy advisor for Gulf Oil, says any relief will be temporary, warning that the cost of diesel will keep the pressure on household budgets.
That's going to infiltrate every nook and cranny of the economy, whether it be groceries. Remember, the farmers have to pay these prices for diesel in its harvest season.
Or whether it be items that you might buy for Christmas instead of being shipped for $10, it's going to be $12.
Closa says the bigger test will come this winter, especially for households in the Northeast that rely on heating oil.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
An investigation into the near crash of a fly-due bi-flight this week is continuing.
Officials say the copilot used an axe to attack the pilot before several passengers intervened to take control of the plane and land it safely.
The investigation is looking at whether the copilot was an extremist.
This weekend, some 2,000 people gathered in Big Bear, California, about 90 miles east of Los Angeles, to mourn the loss of Jackie the Eagle.
Jackie was made famous by a 24/7 livestream. She died in August after being rescued and spending weeks in intensive care.
For member station KVCR, Madison Almond reports.
Bird singers from the Uhab Yutama of San Manuel Nation opened the ceremony at a ski resort that overlooks Big Bear Lake where Jackie fished.
During the music, a plane drew jays for Jackie in the sky.
Many in the crowd wore Jackie t-shirts and clutched Jackie-stuffed animals as they listened to government officials eulogize Jackie.
Leslie Anderberg, who watched the livestream for a decade, summed up the thoughts of many when she said Jackie inspired her.
She gave me peace. She was a very loving mother. I think she just made us better people.
Jackie's remains will be distributed to Native American tribes to be used for religious purposes.
For NPR News, I'm Madison Almond in Big Bear.
Russian forces continued to attack Ukraine this weekend. Strikes on bridges in the capital city of Kyiv have killed at least six people.
Russian's foreign ministry is urging foreign nationals and diplomats to leave the capital, saying forces would continue mass retaliatory strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.
